On the morning the Halvorsen Book Fair opened its doors, the aisles smelled of coffee and cardboard, and agents moved between stalls with the particular hurry of people who have secrets to sell. By afternoon on 14 March 2025, one of those secrets was out. Ellery & Vane has bought the rights to The Glass Cartographer.

The acquisition was confirmed in a joint press statement, issued at the fair and backed by a signed rights agreement. Marguerite Odell, the house's acquisitions director, negotiated the deal. The reported advance is $425,000 for world English-language rights.

Such moments have long been the quiet hinge of publishing, when a manuscript passes from private hope to public object. Ellery & Vane now takes custody of that passage, and with it the work of finding the book its readers.
